steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Augustus established the principate — supreme power while maintaining the appearance of the Republic

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The emperor's power rested on control of the army, the treasury and religious office of pontifex maximus

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Imperial propaganda used coins, statues, architecture and literature to project the emperor's image

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Augustus's Res Gestae was a masterful exercise in self-promotion and political messaging

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: How did Augustus maintain the appearance of the Republic? | Q: Why was army loyalty so important? | Q: How did emperors use propaganda?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: He kept existing offices and institutions but controlled them behind the scenes. He held consulships, tribunician power and the title princeps (first citizen), presenting himself as restoring the Repu | The army was the ultimate source of power — emperors who lost military support were overthrown. The Praetorian Guard could assassinate or install emperors. Donatives secured loyalty. | Coins circulated the emperor's image. Statues showed him as youthful and powerful. Buildings like the Ara Pacis linked him to divine favour. Virgil and Horace celebrated his achievements.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Augustus is the key example — know his methods of maintaining power Discuss the three pillars: army, propaganda and popular provision Use specific propaganda examples: Res Gestae, Ara Pacis, coinage Compare good and bad emperors to show the range of imperial rule The army's political role was crucial — it was not just a military force
